lesson.introduction: Logic studies rules for deciding whether statements and arguments are valid. A proposition is a statement that has a definite truth value: it is either true or false. Questions and commands are not propositions because they do not have a truth value in the same sense.
lesson.core_explanation: Logic studies rules for deciding whether statements and arguments are valid. A proposition is a statement that has a definite truth value: it is either true or false. Questions and commands are not propositions because they do not have a truth value in the same sense. A proposition can be represented by a letter such as P. NOT P reverses the truth value of P. P AND Q is true only when both P and Q are true. P OR Q is false only when both P and Q are false. An implication P → Q is false only when P is true and Q is false.
key_points: A proposition can be represented by a letter such as P.
NOT P reverses the truth value of P.
P AND Q is true only when both P and Q are true.
P OR Q is false only when both P and Q are false.
An implication P → Q is false only when P is true and Q is false.
lesson.worked_example: If P means '12 is even' and Q means '5 is greater than 9', then P is true, Q is false, so P AND Q is false.
lesson.why_it_matters: Logic is useful in mathematics, computer programming, digital circuits and careful everyday reasoning.

lesson.introduction: A linear equation has an unknown whose highest power is one. A quadratic equation has highest power two. Simultaneous equations are solved together because their unknowns must satisfy every equation at the same time.

Substitution of a solution back into the original equations is a useful check.

lesson.introduction: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator, while longitude measures angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Longitude is closely related to local time because Earth rotates through 360° in about 24 hours.
lesson.core_explanation: Latitude measures angular distance north or south of the Equator, while longitude measures angular distance east or west of the Prime Meridian. Longitude is closely related to local time because Earth rotates through 360° in about 24 hours. 15° of longitude corresponds to 1 hour of time difference. 1° corresponds to 4 minutes of time difference. Moving east generally gives a later local time than the reference longitude. Distance along a meridian can be related to angular separation using Earth's circumference model. Read N/S and E/W signs carefully.

lesson.introduction: Electromagnetic induction occurs when the magnetic flux linked with a conductor changes, producing an induced emf. The effect is stronger when the rate of change of flux linkage is greater.
lesson.core_explanation: Electromagnetic induction occurs when the magnetic flux linked with a conductor changes, producing an induced emf. Transformers transfer electrical energy between circuits using changing magnetic fields.
key_points: A relative motion between a magnet and coil can change flux linkage.
Faraday's law links induced emf to the rate of change of flux linkage.
Lenz's law gives the direction of the induced effect.

Transformers transfer electrical energy between circuits using changing magnetic fields.

Heterozygous means two different alleles. Mendel's work established important patterns of inheritance.
